segments.text: He lives through the atomic bomb at Hiroshima. Then he goes home. Home is Nagasaki.
No chance. Not both. Let's go look.
August {1945|nineteen forty-five}. Name: Tsutomu Yamaguchi. He is {29|twenty-nine}, an engineer, ending a work trip in Hiroshima. A flash. He is under two miles away.
He is burned. His eardrums are burst. He shelters for the night. Next day, he goes home.
Three days on, bandaged, he is back at work in Nagasaki, telling his boss about the bomb. His boss doesn't believe him.
Then the same white light fills the room. He lives again.
He lived to {93|ninety-three}. In {2009|two thousand nine}, Japan certified him as a survivor of both. Officially, the only one.
He used those years to ask the world to give up the bomb. I was wrong. Case closed.
